cards.issue_title: CIBIL score box forces an exact number instead of a range dropdown
summary_4_lines: The CIBIL score box on Explore banks is a type-in field. It asks for one exact number.
They said that is the problem: it forces the exact score.
They want a dropdown of score windows (for example 750 to 780), not a vague “approximate” with a star at the bottom.
They kept clicking that same box while arguing buckets, bank breakouts, and Amazon-style typeahead.
cards.pinpoint: On Explore banks, the CIBIL score control is a free-text box that forces an exact number; they said the problem is that it forces the exact score and they need a dropdown of score windows (e.g. 750–780, 730–750) instead of typing an exact score, and they rejected calling the result approximate with a star footnote.
cards.on_screen_object: CIBIL score* text box (#hlc-cibil, placeholder 780) in the Loan inputs form, plus its About CIBIL score info button
quotes_sample: You are forcing me to tell the exact score.
No. Here, we need a drop down.
And here we give a range but do not give a drop down.
related_discussion_one_liners: Coarse bands already in people’s heads (“Average, high,” “700 plus is excellent”) — they want numeric windows, not those words.
Bucket size: 10-point ranges vs 5-point (“with 55” / 5–5); ten points “don’t change,” five-point makes the list bigger; finer buckets near “900 top score” make it long.
Negotiation: “I have 776 also. Show me the offer of 780”; ten points here and there should still work without throwing so much that 776/778 is ignored.
Bank-specific breakouts are not parallel (one bank 800–810, another 850–812); they also debate “Minimum Sibyl Score” vs exact on the same box, and stress about knowing 5–10 points.
Amazon typeahead analogy: type 766 and dropdowns open; type F and it freezes; either select a dropdown or type a range — do not mix both in a confusing way.
